newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNI FOCUS -- low volatility, Fed held steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNI FOCUS -- low volatility, Fed held steady.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds, which have been almost inert as traders waited to see if the Federal Reserve would raise rates, saw prices firm slightly but volatility barely budged after it opted to stay the course.

The overall municipal market market edged up nearly an eighth of a point, a municipal analyst said, noting much of the firmness was achieved late in the afternoon though he described activity as extremely light.
High grades through the intermediate range climbed about two basis points, with some rising three basis points. Dollar bonds strengthened about an eighth of a point, he added.
Referring to the Fed's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, a trader said: "I guess it wasn't unexpected, but it makes the market a little boring."
Traders said that from here on out, they will be poring over the latest economic reports as they try to figure out what the central bank's policy-makers will do when they next meet in early July.

And some market participants were disappointed that the Federal Reserve failed to raise federal funds by 25 basis points. "You would have had the best of both worlds. You would have been ahead of the curve and all the economic numbers for the last week have been positive."

The deal of the day, Nevada's sale of $285 million of general obligation bonds, went well, traders said, noting that even though this is a fairly large offering for the state, the paucity of supply boosted demand. The bonds were won by Smith Barney with a true interest cost of 5.53 percent.
"New issue pricing was firm through the list," said the municipal analyst.
Wednesday's calender includes $1.07 billion of negotiated sales plus $185.1 million of competitive sales.

The leading negotiated sale will be New York City's approximately $740 million offering. The city sold a total of $206 million of bonds to retail investors in a presale period, closing out the three longest maturities--2014, 2015 and 2016--as well as 2011.
Though New York City fell short of a near-record total of $304 million set in early April, a city official said: I would say this is a healthy, average order period."
In the secondary market, Oregon State Department Administrative Services of May 2024, which carry a 5.8 percent coupon, were bid at 99-3/4, down one-quarter of a point.
And Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of February 2027, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 99, unchanged.

June municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade slipped five ticks to 116-22/32, while the June Treasury bond futures eased two ticks to 109-27/32. This left the MOB spread at a strong plus 219 ticks.
